summary.method: All units with compile completed and not withdrawn were audited in factory-v5 (highest existing release) and factory-v6 (the identity_release named in state). For each, the task.json public section and the public asset text were read, excluding private/. The root auditor read the IDEA and LIT tasks in full; two read-only sub-auditors read the EXP and WRITE tasks, and the EXP leak excerpts were re-verified with grep. A mechanical scan found none of the following in any public text: the target title, author surnames, target arXiv ids, repository or user names, or coined method names (ActNet, GETS, SYMPOL, VSD, LOO-StabCP, MILE, GyroBN, SensPB, IDI, IPA).
summary.note: Low-level title-word overlaps in clear WRITE tasks come from describing the method and are omitted. Many cutoffs equal the target's v1 date; these are flagged only where the text explicitly says the date is the target's.

findings.excerpt: The network architectures specified and evaluated in the reviewed machine-learning works (§2) build on Eq. (K). Counted from the formulas **(maintainer)**, that is the only form in §1.2 with O(d^2) distinct inner functions. The library does not include an evaluated network design built on the other forms.
findings.why: This maintainer-derived gap points directly at the target's contribution, a network built on the Laczkovich single-outer-function form (ActNet). It is worded as neutral, but it steers strongly.

findings.excerpt: Forms (L), (S), (Z1) and (Z2) tie the inner terms together through a shared inner function or a shared outer function and scalar weights. Their numbers of distinct univariate functions grow linearly in `d` (or are constant).
findings.why: This maintainer analysis reinforces the same steering.

findings.why: The research question states the target's contribution direction: an MoE ensemble of temperature-scaling calibrators driven by graph-structural inputs (GETS).

findings.excerpt: Excluded from EXP: soft/discretised soft tree baselines, shared-architecture, batch-size and weight-decay ablations, continuous actions, LunarLander, MiniGrid and case study, A2C, VIPER, runtime claims, and weight averaging

findings.excerpt: This report does not say how to obtain a small, hard, axis-aligned tree policy whose deployed behaviour is exactly the behaviour that was optimised. It leaves that question open.
findings.why: The report gives a very detailed account of GradTree, the target authors' own supervised predecessor (SYMPOL is GradTree trained directly with on-policy RL), plus PPO, AdamW and SWA entries. Combined with this open problem, it steers toward the target method. The target itself is not stated.

findings.excerpt: Also state any components you add for training stability and any optimiser or regularisation choices you consider essential.
findings.why: A mild hint that the target relies on stability components and specific optimiser choices.

findings.excerpt: Then identify the open gap: where performance or behaviour can be lost between the model that training optimises and the interpretable tree that is finally deployed
findings.why: The LIT task hands the solver the target's gap conclusion: information loss between the optimised and the deployed tree (title: 'Mitigating Information Loss ... via Direct Optimization'). F01 also says: 'Identify the open gap between what is optimised and what is deployed.'

findings.excerpt: IDEA: the neutral problem statement fixed by the unit scope. It states goals and constraints only, with no objective, divergence, classifier role or gradient estimator of the target.
findings.why: Same negative-disclosure pattern as the withdrawn QMtrW8Ej98 IDEA. It tells the solver that the target method has a specific objective, a divergence, a classifier role and a gradient estimator. That is the core of VSD: a KL-based variational search distribution with a class-probability classifier and a score-function gradient.

findings.excerpt: The scope explicitly permits describing classifier-based BO, adaptive-sampling design, score-function gradients and probabilistic reparameterisation as background. None is described as adapted by the source paper, and no source results are included.
findings.why: It names the background families the scope singled out and implies that the source paper adapts them. This hints at which ingredients the target combines.

findings.excerpt: The counterfactual route needs the noise values of the observed anomalous sample. When the mechanisms are fitted from normal-period data, these values come from the fitted mechanisms (R4, R5). ... One work argues that analysing outliers probes fitted regression models in low-density regions (R6).
findings.why: This maintainer synthesis lines up the target's key insight: counterfactual abduction at out-of-distribution anomalous points is unreliable, so the fix should be assessed with in-distribution interventions. It is derived from background works, but it steers.

findings.excerpt: how to *assess*, with an SCM fitted only on normal-period data, whether restoring a candidate to a normal value would have removed the target anomaly.
findings.why: The task narrows exactly to the target's fix-condition problem. That is legitimate framing on its own, but together with R8 it narrows strongly.

findings.field_or_line: Research question items 1-2; required sections "## Anomaly condition" and "## Fix condition"
findings.excerpt: 2. **Fix condition.** How do existing methods decide whether resetting a candidate node to usual behaviour would have prevented the target anomaly? Distinguish approaches based on counterfactuals (with abduction or reconstruction of noise/exogenous variables), approaches based on interventions ... Also identify methods that do not assess this condition at all.
findings.why: 'Anomaly condition' and 'Fix condition' are the target paper's own coined root-cause definition. Its introduction reads: 'We define root cause as nodes that satisfy two key conditions: (1) Anomaly condition ... Fix condition ... the fix condition is often overlooked'. Its key contribution is the counterfactual-versus-intervention contrast. The review is organised around the target's framework and gap.

findings.excerpt: A finite-amplitude bias is expected because the update uses g(x) while the linearisation uses B = [0;3].
findings.why: It states an expected outcome that bears on the H2/H4 residuals. The expectation is maintainer-derived.
